text: Before any other MPI call, call {{c1::\(\mathrm{MPI\_Init}\) }}. When you are done with MPI, call {{c2::\(\mathrm{MPI\_Finalize}\) }}.
extra: No MPI functions before Init or after Finalize. You can pass NULL,NULL to Init if you skip argc and argv.

text: In {{c1::\(\mathrm{MPI\_COMM\_WORLD}\) }}, {{c2::\(\mathrm{MPI\_Comm\_size}\) }} tells you how many processes started, and {{c3::\(\mathrm{MPI\_Comm\_rank}\) }} gives this process its ID in \(0..p-1\).
extra: A communicator is the set of processes that can message each other. Init builds that default world communicator for you.

text: A receive only wakes up when the message hits the same communicator, the same {{c1::tag}}, and the expected {{c2::source}} rank.
extra: The send dest must also be this receiver. Buffers need a matching type and a recv count at least as large as the send.

text: Only the {{c1::receiver}} may use wildcards like \(\mathrm{MPI\_ANY\_SOURCE}\). Senders name a real rank and a nonnegative tag, and there is {{c2::no}} communicator wildcard.
extra: \(\mathrm{MPI\_ANY\_TAG}\) is also recv-only. MPI pushes messages; a sender cannot pull from a wildcard dest.

text: After \(\mathrm{MPI\_Recv}\) with \(\mathrm{MPI\_ANY\_SOURCE}\), read {{c1::\(\mathrm{status.MPI\_SOURCE}\) }} for who sent it and {{c2::\(\mathrm{status.MPI\_TAG}\) }} for the actual tag.
extra: Pass a real \(\mathrm{MPI\_Status}\), not \(\mathrm{MPI\_STATUS\_IGNORE}\), if you need those fields. Study-guide managers use this after any-source recv.

text: To learn how many elements arrived, call {{c1::\(\mathrm{MPI\_Get\_count}\) }} with the status and datatype. That count is {{c2::not}} a direct member of \(\mathrm{MPI\_Status}\).
extra: Count depends on the datatype, so MPI computes it on demand as bytes received over bytes per object.

text: Messages from one sender to one receiver are {{c1::non-overtaking}}: the first send is available before the second. Messages from {{c2::different}} senders have no required arrival order.
extra: A recv loop in rank order can stall if a high-rank worker finishes first. Prefer \(\mathrm{MPI\_ANY\_SOURCE}\) when finish order is unknown.

text: \(\mathrm{MPI\_Recv}\) {{c1::always blocks}} until a matching message arrives. A missing or mismatched send can make the process {{c2::hang}} forever.
extra: \(\mathrm{MPI\_Send}\) may also block if the implementation does not buffer. A buffered send with no matching recv can lose the message.

text: In typical MPI setups, only rank {{c1::0}} may read stdin. Every rank can write stdout, but multi-rank printf order is {{c2::nondeterministic}}.
extra: For ordered output, send strings to rank 0 and print there, as in the greetings program.

text: A tag on \(\mathrm{MPI\_Send}\) and \(\mathrm{MPI\_Recv}\) lets you {{c1::distinguish otherwise identical messages}}, like print floats versus compute floats.
extra: Matching needs equal tags unless the receiver uses \(\mathrm{MPI\_ANY\_TAG}\). The study guide flags tags the way A2 uses them.

text: For a collective, {{c1::all}} processes in the communicator must call the same function. Collectives match by communicator and {{c2::call order}}, not by tags.
extra: Arguments must be compatible, such as the same root. Matching Reduce with Recv is erroneous and can hang or crash.

text: \(\mathrm{MPI\_Bcast}\) sends the data from {{c1::the root}} to {{c2::every process}} in the communicator.
extra: Typical pattern: rank 0 reads parameters, then Bcast so every rank has them. The buffer is in on root and out on the others.

text: \(\mathrm{MPI\_Reduce}\) combines each process input with an operator such as \(\mathrm{MPI\_SUM}\) and stores the result {{c1::only on the destination rank}}.
extra: Every rank still passes an output buffer. With count greater than 1, arrays reduce elementwise. Study-guide Q1: local sums, then one Reduce.

text: \(\mathrm{MPI\_Allreduce}\) is like Reduce, but the combined result lands on {{c1::every process}} in the communicator.
extra: Use it when all ranks need the global value for further work. Same operator, datatype, and count rules as Reduce, with no dest argument.

text: On a slow network, summing \(g(a[i])\) over a large distributed array: each rank should {{c1::sum its local block}}, then combine with {{c2::one \(\mathrm{MPI\_Reduce}\) }}.
extra: Study-guide practice Q1 answer D. Allreduce after every element, or one message per element, is too chatty on a slow link.

text: When \(\mathrm{MPI\_Send}\) returns, the send buffer is {{c1::safe to reuse}}. You still do {{c2::not}} know whether the message has already been delivered.
extra: Small messages are often buffered. Large ones may block until transmission can start. The cutoff is implementation-dependent.
